pinyin: dà dǎn jiǎ shè, xiǎo xīn qiú zhèng
natural: hypothesise boldly, verify carefully

meaning.en: A motto of scientific method: put forward daring hypotheses, but test them with careful evidence.
meaning.zh: 治学和研究的方法口诀：敢于提出大胆的假设，但要用细致的证据加以验证。

equivalents: be bold in conjecture, careful in proof
dare to hypothesise, take care to verify

examples.zh: 导师常说，做研究要大胆假设，小心求证。
examples.en: My supervisor often says that research means bold hypotheses and careful verification.

examples.zh: 大胆假设，小心求证，这是科学探索的基本态度。
examples.en: Bold hypotheses and careful verification are the basic attitude of scientific inquiry.

usage.en: Strongly associated with the scholar Hu Shi (胡适), who promoted it as a method for research; quoted in schools and academic writing. Exact first wording and place of publication vary between accounts, so no origin is given.
usage.zh: 与学者胡适关系最密切，他曾大力提倡这一治学方法，常见于学校和学术文章。最初的确切措辞和出处说法不一，故不标出处。

text: 多研究些问题，少谈些主义
pinyin: duō yán jiū xiē wèn tí, shǎo tán xiē zhǔ yì
literal: more · study · some · problems, less · talk · some · -isms
natural: study more problems, talk less about -isms

meaning.en: Hu Shi's call to tackle concrete problems rather than argue over grand doctrines.
meaning.zh: 胡适的主张：多研究具体的实际问题，少空谈抽象的主义。

examples.zh: 开会时有人说：“多研究些问题，少谈些主义。”
examples.en: At the meeting someone said, 'study more problems and talk less about -isms'.

examples.zh: 这篇评论提醒读者多研究些问题，少谈些主义。
examples.en: This commentary reminds readers to study more problems and talk less about -isms.

origin.source: 胡适《多研究些问题，少谈些主义》，《每周评论》（1919年7月）

story.en: Hu Shi published the essay in the journal 'Weekly Review' (《每周评论》) in July 1919, arguing that reform should begin with specific problems rather than imported -isms.
story.zh: 1919年7月，胡适在《每周评论》发表此文，主张改革应从具体问题入手，而不是空谈外来的“主义”。

usage.en: Both the title and the thesis of an essay in a 1919 debate with Li Dazhao and others on 'problems and -isms' (问题与主义). Today it is quoted, sometimes approvingly and sometimes critically, in discussions of pragmatism versus ideology.
usage.zh: 既是文章标题，也是文中主旨，出自1919年围绕“问题与主义”的论争。今天在讨论实用主义与意识形态时被引用，褒贬不一。

text: 不在沉默中爆发，就在沉默中灭亡
pinyin: bù zài chén mò zhōng bào fā, jiù zài chén mò zhōng miè wáng
literal: not · in · silence · within · erupt, then · in · silence · within · perish
natural: if you do not erupt in silence, you perish in silence

meaning.en: Lu Xun's warning that people who stay silent under oppression will either burst out in action or be destroyed.
meaning.zh: 鲁迅的警句：面对压迫一味沉默，不是奋起反抗，就是走向灭亡。

equivalents: speak up or be wiped out

examples.zh: 演讲者引用鲁迅的话：“不在沉默中爆发，就在沉默中灭亡。”
examples.en: The speaker quoted Lu Xun: 'Erupt in silence or perish in silence.'

examples.zh: 面对不公，不在沉默中爆发，就在沉默中灭亡。
examples.en: Faced with injustice, you either erupt or perish in silence.

story.en: Lu Xun wrote the essay in April 1926 after the 18 March shooting of demonstrators in Beijing, including his student Liu Hezhen; the line reads 'Silence, silence! If we do not erupt in silence, we perish in silence.'
story.zh: 1926年4月，鲁迅在“三一八”惨案后写下此文纪念学生刘和珍，原句是“沉默啊，沉默啊！不在沉默中爆发，就在沉默中灭亡。”

usage.en: Often quoted in speeches, editorials and student essays as a call to speak up. Literary, strong in tone.
usage.zh: 常见于演讲、社论和学生作文，用来呼吁人们站出来发声。书面语，语气强烈。

pinyin: chī de shì cǎo, jǐ chū de shì nǎi
natural: what goes in is grass, what comes out is milk

meaning.en: Giving a great deal in return for very little; selfless dedication, like a cow that eats grass and gives milk.
meaning.zh: 所得很少而贡献很大，形容无私奉献，像牛吃的是草、产出的是奶。

equivalents: give far more than you take

examples.zh: 老教授一生清贫，吃的是草，挤出的是奶。
examples.en: The old professor lived frugally all his life, eating grass and giving milk.

examples.zh: 他们那一代人吃的是草，挤出的是奶，默默建设着国家。
examples.en: Their generation took little and gave much, quietly building the country.

usage.en: Usually linked with Lu Xun, who is often quoted as comparing himself to an ox ('I eat grass, and what I squeeze out is milk and blood'), and with his famous couplet 俯首甘为孺子牛. The exact wording and source of the prose quotation are not firmly established, so no origin is given. Praise for selfless devotion.
usage.zh: 通常与鲁迅联系在一起，常被引述为他以牛自比（“吃的是草，挤出来的是牛奶、血”），也让人想到“俯首甘为孺子牛”。这段话的确切措辞和出处并无定论，故不标出处。多用于赞扬无私奉献。

pinyin: yī gè dōu bù kuān shù
natural: not forgive a single one

meaning.en: Lu Xun's defiant statement near the end of his life that he would forgive none of his enemies.
meaning.zh: 鲁迅晚年的名言，表示决不原谅任何一个与他为敌的人。

examples.zh: 他固执地说：“一个都不宽恕。”
examples.en: He stubbornly declared, 'I will forgive not one of them.'

examples.zh: 鲁迅那句“一个都不宽恕”常被后人引用。
examples.en: Lu Xun's line 'not forgive a single one' is often quoted by later generations.

story.en: In the 1936 essay 'Death' Lu Xun wrote that when asked for forgiveness at his death he would answer, 'Let them hate me; I too will forgive not one of them' (让他们怨恨去，我也一个都不宽恕).
story.zh: 鲁迅在1936年的《死》中写道：“让他们怨恨去，我也一个都不宽恕。”

usage.en: Quoted to express an uncompromising stance towards enemies or wrongdoers, sometimes humorously for personal grudges. Readers often take it out of context: it concerns Lu Xun's own enemies in a deathbed-style reflection.
usage.zh: 用来表示对敌人或恶行毫不妥协，有时也半开玩笑地用于个人恩怨。常被断章取义：原文是鲁迅对自己论敌的临终式感想。

pinyin: fèi è pō lài yīng gāi huǎn xíng
natural: 'fair play' should be put off for now

meaning.en: Lu Xun's argument that 'fair play' should not yet be extended to ruthless opponents, who would only take advantage of it.
meaning.zh: 鲁迅的观点：对凶狠的对手不能先讲“费厄泼赖”（公平竞争），否则只会被对方利用。

equivalents: don't play fair with those who don't

examples.zh: 鲁迅写过一篇杂文，题目就是《论“费厄泼赖”应该缓行》，费厄泼赖应该缓行的观点引起不少争论。
examples.en: Lu Xun's essay on why 'fair play' should be postponed, with the thesis 费厄泼赖应该缓行, caused much debate.

examples.zh: 历史课上，老师讲解了费厄泼赖应该缓行一文的写作背景。
examples.en: In history class the teacher explained the background of the essay 'Fair play should be put off'.

origin.source: 鲁迅《论“费厄泼赖”应该缓行》

story.en: Lu Xun wrote the essay in December 1925, responding to Lin Yutang's call for fair play; it was later collected in 'The Grave' (《坟》).
story.zh: 鲁迅1925年12月针对林语堂提倡“费厄泼赖”而作此文，后收入《坟》。

usage.en: 费厄泼赖 is a transliteration of the English 'fair play'. The essay is aimed at a particular 1925 political situation, and later readers discuss how far its advice applies; it is cited both for and against ruthless tactics. The famous image in it is beating the 'dog in the water' (落水狗).
usage.zh: “费厄泼赖”是英语 fair play 的音译。该文针对1925年的具体政治局势，后人对其适用范围看法不一，既有人引用也有人批评。文中著名的比喻是“痛打落水狗”。

pinyin: zhōng guó de jǐ liáng
natural: the backbone of China

meaning.en: Lu Xun's phrase for the tireless, self-sacrificing people who carry the nation on their shoulders.
meaning.zh: 鲁迅用来称颂埋头苦干、舍身为民、支撑民族的人。

examples.zh: 科学家们被称为“中国的脊梁”。
examples.en: Scientists have been called 'the backbone of China'.

examples.zh: 这套丛书讲述了中国的脊梁们的故事。
examples.en: The book series tells the stories of the people who are the backbone of China.

origin.source: 鲁迅《中国人失掉自信力了吗》

story.en: In this 1934 essay Lu Xun listed those who work doggedly, fight hard, plead for the people and sacrifice themselves, and concluded: 'these are the backbone of China'.
story.zh: 鲁迅1934年在此文中列举埋头苦干、拼命硬干、为民请命、舍身求法的人，称“这就是中国的脊梁”。

usage.en: Now a stock tribute to people who shoulder the nation's burdens, often in news headlines and book titles. A noun phrase rather than a set idiom.
usage.zh: 如今是对担当民族重任者的固定赞辞，常见于新闻标题和书名。这是名词性短语，不是成语。

pinyin: sī xiǎng zì yóu, jiān róng bìng bāo
literal: thought · free, embrace · accommodate · together · include
natural: freedom of thought, inclusive of all views

meaning.en: The guiding principle of Cai Yuanpei's reforms at Peking University: let different schools of thought coexist freely.
meaning.zh: 蔡元培改革北京大学的办学方针：不同学派的思想自由并存，互相包容。

equivalents: free thought and tolerance of all schools

examples.zh: 校长在致辞中强调大学应当思想自由，兼容并包。
examples.en: In his speech the president stressed that a university should embrace free thought and tolerate all views.

examples.zh: 北大的传统常被概括为思想自由，兼容并包。
examples.en: Peking University's tradition is often summed up as free thought and inclusiveness.

usage.en: Closely tied to Cai Yuanpei, president of Peking University from 1917; the exact two-part wording is a later summary of his stated principles, so no origin is given. 兼容并包 is also a variant of the idiom 兼容并蓄, but this slogan is a separate set phrase. Often quoted about universities and academic freedom.
usage.zh: 与1917年起任北京大学校长的蔡元培紧密相连；这八字是对他办学主张的后世概括，故不标出处。“兼容并包”也是成语“兼容并蓄”的异形，但这一口号是另一个固定说法。常用于谈论大学和学术自由。

text: 独立之精神，自由之思想
pinyin: dú lì zhī jīng shén, zì yóu zhī sī xiǎng
natural: the spirit of independence, the thought of freedom

meaning.en: Chen Yinke's ideal for scholars: to think independently and freely, whatever the circumstances.
meaning.zh: 陈寅恪对学者的期许：不依附外力，独立自由地思考。

equivalents: independence of spirit, freedom of thought

examples.zh: 毕业典礼上，校长引用了“独立之精神，自由之思想”。
examples.en: At the graduation ceremony the president quoted 'independence of spirit, freedom of thought'.

examples.zh: 学者应当保持独立之精神，自由之思想。
examples.en: A scholar should keep independence of spirit and freedom of thought.

origin.source: 陈寅恪《海宁王静安先生纪念碑铭》

story.en: Chen Yinke wrote the inscription for the memorial to the scholar Wang Guowei at Tsinghua in 1929: 'Only this independent spirit and free thought will last as long as heaven and earth.'
story.zh: 1929年，陈寅恪为清华园王国维纪念碑撰写碑铭，称“惟此独立之精神，自由之思想，历千万祀，与天壤而同久”。

usage.en: Widely quoted in discussions of academic freedom, in school speeches and in essays. The inscription also continues that these ideals will 'last as long as heaven and earth'. Literary and solemn.
usage.zh: 常用于谈论学术自由，见于学校演讲和作文。碑文接着说这种精神“与天壤而同久，共三光而永光”。书面语，庄重。

text: 大学者，非谓有大楼之谓也，有大师之谓也
pinyin: dà xué zhě, fēi wèi yǒu dà lóu zhī wèi yě, yǒu dà shī zhī wèi yě
literal: great · learning · -er, not · say · have · big · buildings · 's · saying · -, have · great · masters · 's · saying
natural: a university is not about big buildings but about great masters

meaning.en: Mei Yiqi's remark that what makes a university great is its eminent teachers, not its buildings.
meaning.zh: 梅贻琦的名言：大学之所以为大学，不在于有高楼大厦，而在于有学识卓著的大师。

equivalents: a university is its scholars, not its buildings

examples.zh: 校长说：“大学者，非谓有大楼之谓也，有大师之谓也。”
examples.en: The president said, 'A university is not about big buildings but about great masters.'

examples.zh: 大学者，非谓有大楼之谓也，有大师之谓也，这话常被用来强调师资的重要。
examples.en: The saying that a university is not about big buildings but great masters is often used to stress the importance of faculty.

origin.source: 梅贻琦清华大学校长就职演说

story.en: Mei Yiqi said this in his inaugural address as president of Tsinghua University in December 1931.
story.zh: 1931年12月，梅贻琦在就任清华大学校长的演说中说出这句话。

usage.en: The usual wording is 所谓大学者，非谓有大楼之谓也，有大师之谓也. Often quoted in education debates and university promotions, sometimes to criticise spending on buildings.
usage.zh: 通行的说法是“所谓大学者，非谓有大楼之谓也，有大师之谓也”。常见于教育讨论和高校宣传，有时用来批评一味盖楼。

text: 华北之大，已经安放不得一张平静的书桌了
pinyin: huá běi zhī dà, yǐ jīng ān fàng bù dé yī zhāng píng jìng de shū zhuō le
literal: North China · 's · vastness, already · place · cannot · one · -piece · peaceful · 's · desk · (particle)
natural: vast as North China is, it can no longer hold one peaceful desk

meaning.en: A line from the student movement of 1935: with Japanese pressure on North China, students could no longer study in peace.
meaning.zh: 1935年学生运动中的名句：日本侵逼华北，学生已经无法安心读书。

equivalents: there is no longer a quiet place to study
not even room for a peaceful desk

examples.zh: 历史书引用“华北之大，已经安放不得一张平静的书桌了”来描写一二·九运动。
examples.en: History books quote 'vast as North China is, it can no longer hold one peaceful desk' to describe the December Ninth Movement.

examples.zh: 纪念会上，同学们朗读了“华北之大，已经安放不得一张平静的书桌了”。
examples.en: At the commemoration students read out 'North China, vast as it is, cannot hold one peaceful desk'.

usage.en: Associated with Beijing students' appeals during the December Ninth Movement of 1935. Accounts differ on exactly which manifesto first carried the sentence, so no origin is given. Today quoted when talking about the cost of war to education.
usage.zh: 与1935年一二·九运动中北平学生的呼吁相联系。具体出自哪份宣言说法不一，故不标出处。今天常用于谈战争对教育的冲击。

text: 青年要立志做大事，不可立志做大官
pinyin: qīng nián yào lì zhì zuò dà shì, bù kě lì zhì zuò dà guān
literal: youth · should · set ambition · do · big · things, not · may · set ambition · be · big · official
natural: young people should aim to do great things, not to hold high office

meaning.en: Advice to the young to pursue meaningful achievements rather than rank and position.
meaning.zh: 劝勉青年要追求有意义的事业，而不是官位和地位。

equivalents: aim to achieve, not to rank
do great things, don't chase high office

examples.zh: 毕业典礼上，老师引用了“青年要立志做大事，不可立志做大官”。
examples.en: At the graduation, the teacher quoted 'young people should aim to do great things, not to hold high office'.

examples.zh: 他把青年要立志做大事，不可立志做大官写在书桌前。
examples.en: He wrote 'youth should aim to do great things, not to hold high office' above his desk.

usage.en: Commonly attributed to Sun Yat-sen's talks to students in the 1920s, and widely used in school and civic education. Exact occasion and wording vary, so no origin is given.
usage.zh: 通常认为出自孙中山对青年学生的演讲，广泛用于学校和公民教育。具体场合和措辞说法不一，故不标出处。

text: 好铁不打钉，好男不当兵
pinyin: hǎo tiě bù dǎ dīng, hǎo nán bù dāng bīng
literal: good · iron · not · make · nails, good · man · not · be · soldier
natural: good iron isn't made into nails, a good man doesn't become a soldier

meaning.en: An old folk saying reflecting the low status of soldiers in the era of warlords and press-gangs: capable people avoid army life.
meaning.zh: 旧时民间俗语，反映军阀混战、抓壮丁年代人们对当兵的轻视：有出息的人不去当兵。

examples.zh: 老人们还记得“好铁不打钉，好男不当兵”的说法。
examples.en: The old folks still remember the saying 'good iron isn't made into nails, a good man doesn't become a soldier'.

examples.zh: 好铁不打钉，好男不当兵，这种旧观念如今已大为改变。
examples.en: The old view that a good man doesn't become a soldier has changed greatly.

usage.en: A dated folk saying; today military service is widely respected and the saying is cited as a historical attitude, often with a contrast such as 'now good men join the army'. No origin is known, so none is given.
usage.zh: 已经过时的民间俗语。今天参军受到普遍尊重，这句话多作为旧观念被提及。出处不详，故不标出处。

pinyin: huá rén yǔ gǒu bù dé rù nèi
literal: Chinese · people · and · dogs · not · allowed · enter · inside
natural: no Chinese or dogs allowed

meaning.en: The notice said to have stood at the entrance of a Shanghai park in the foreign concessions, a symbol of discrimination against Chinese people.
meaning.zh: 据说曾立于上海租界公园门口的告示，成为歧视华人的象征。

examples.zh: 历史课上讲到“华人与狗不得入内”的牌子引发的愤怒。
examples.en: The history lesson covered the anger caused by the sign 'no Chinese or dogs allowed'.

examples.zh: 电影里出现了“华人与狗不得入内”的场景。
examples.en: The film features a scene with the sign 'no Chinese or dogs allowed'.

usage.en: Historians dispute the exact wording. Park regulations at the Huangpu Park (Shanghai Public Garden) are recorded as banning dogs and bicycles, and separately as barring Chinese from entering, but whether one sign combined the two is debated. The phrase nevertheless became a lasting symbol of semi-colonial humiliation in textbooks, film and memory. Use with care and treat as historical reference.
usage.zh: 具体措辞学界有争议。黄浦公园（上海公家花园）的规定记载中，有禁止狗和自行车入内的条文，也有不准华人入内的条文，但是否合写在同一块牌子上仍有争论。无论如何，这句话已成为教科书、电影和集体记忆中半殖民地屈辱的象征。使用时宜谨慎，作历史引用。

text: 一个主义，一个党，一个领袖
pinyin: yī gè zhǔ yì, yī gè dǎng, yī gè lǐng xiù
literal: one · doctrine, one · party, one · leader
natural: one doctrine, one party, one leader

meaning.en: A 1930s Kuomintang slogan for single-party rule under one ideology and one leader, Chiang Kai-shek.
meaning.zh: 1930年代国民党的口号，主张在一个主义、一个政党、一个领袖之下实行集中统治。

equivalents: one ideology, one party, one leader

examples.zh: 历史教材介绍了“一个主义，一个党，一个领袖”的口号。
examples.en: The history textbook introduces the slogan 'one doctrine, one party, one leader'.

examples.zh: 论文分析了一个主义，一个党，一个领袖这一口号的形成背景。
examples.en: The paper analyses the background of the slogan 'one doctrine, one party, one leader'.

usage.en: A historical political slogan, often studied in connection with the period of 'party rule' and with leader-cult trends of the 1930s. Its exact first user is not firmly established, so no origin is given. Neutral historical reference.
usage.zh: 历史政治口号，常与“以党治国”及1930年代领袖崇拜思潮一并研究。最先由谁提出并无定论，故不标出处。作中性的历史引用。

pinyin: guó jiā zhì shàng, mín zú zhì shàng
natural: the nation first, the people first

meaning.en: A wartime slogan of the Second Sino-Japanese War: national interests outrank personal and partisan ones.
meaning.zh: 抗日战争时期的口号：国家和民族的利益高于个人和党派的利益。

examples.zh: 抗战时期，“国家至上，民族至上”的标语随处可见。
examples.en: During the war of resistance the slogan 'the nation first, the people first' was seen everywhere.

examples.zh: 他在演讲中重提国家至上，民族至上的精神。
examples.en: In his speech he recalled the spirit of 'nation first, people first'.

usage.en: A wartime mobilisation slogan of the Nationalist government, often paired with 军事第一，胜利第一. Today used as a historical reference or in patriotic appeals. Exact origin is not given.
usage.zh: 国民政府的战时动员口号，常与“军事第一，胜利第一”并提。今天多作历史引用或用于爱国号召。不标出处。

pinyin: jūn shì dì yī, shèng lì dì yī
natural: military affairs first, victory first

meaning.en: A wartime slogan of the Second Sino-Japanese War: every effort must serve the war and final victory.
meaning.zh: 抗日战争时期的口号：一切工作都要服从战争，为取得最后胜利服务。

examples.zh: 战时的标语写着“军事第一，胜利第一”。
examples.en: The wartime banner read 'military first, victory first'.

examples.zh: 展览里有一张“军事第一，胜利第一”的宣传画。
examples.en: The exhibition has a poster saying 'military first, victory first'.

usage.en: A wartime mobilisation slogan of the Nationalist government, usually quoted together with 国家至上，民族至上. A historical reference only; no origin is given.
usage.zh: 国民政府的战时动员口号，常与“国家至上，民族至上”连用。仅作历史引用，不标出处。

pinyin: kàng zhàn jiàn guó
natural: resist and rebuild the nation

meaning.en: The wartime policy of fighting Japan while building the nation, set out in the 1938 programme of the Kuomintang.
meaning.zh: 战时方针：一面抗击日本侵略，一面建设国家，见于1938年国民党的纲领。

examples.zh: 政府提出“抗战建国”，要求一面作战一面建设。
examples.en: The government put forward 'resistance and national reconstruction', calling for fighting and building at once.

examples.zh: 展览介绍了抗战建国时期的西迁大学。
examples.en: The exhibition covers the universities that moved west during the 'resist and rebuild' period.

origin.source: 《抗战建国纲领》（1938年4月，国民党临时全国代表大会）

story.en: The Kuomintang's Extraordinary National Congress at Wuhan adopted the Programme of Armed Resistance and National Reconstruction in April 1938.
story.zh: 1938年4月，国民党临时全国代表大会在武汉通过《抗战建国纲领》。

usage.en: A formal historical term for the wartime national programme. The Kuomintang's Extraordinary National Congress adopted the Programme of Armed Resistance and National Reconstruction in April 1938.
usage.zh: 指战时国策的正式历史术语。1938年4月，国民党临时全国代表大会通过《抗战建国纲领》。

pinyin: bù zuò wáng guó nú
natural: refuse to be slaves of a conquered nation

meaning.en: A patriotic cry of the war against Japan: better to resist than to live under foreign occupation.
meaning.zh: 抗日战争时期的爱国呼声：宁可抵抗，也不甘心在外族统治下生活。

equivalents: better to fight than live under occupation

examples.zh: 游行的学生高喊“不做亡国奴”。
examples.en: The marching students shouted 'we will not be slaves of a conquered nation'.

examples.zh: 抗战歌曲里反复唱着不做亡国奴。
examples.en: Wartime songs repeatedly sing of refusing to be slaves of a conquered nation.

usage.en: Widespread slogan of the 1930s and 1940s, used by many groups and not tied to a single author or party. Today used in historical context, or figuratively, in patriotic appeals.
usage.zh: 1930至1940年代广泛流行的口号，许多团体使用，不属于某一作者或政党。今天多用于历史语境，或作爱国号召。

pinyin: qīn ài jīng chéng
natural: affection and sincerity

meaning.en: The motto of the Whampoa Military Academy, urging comrades to be close, loving, devoted and sincere.
meaning.zh: 黄埔军校的校训，勉励同学亲密、友爱、专一、真诚。

examples.zh: 黄埔军校的校训是“亲爱精诚”。
examples.en: The motto of the Whampoa Military Academy is 'affection and sincerity'.

examples.zh: 毕业典礼上，学员们齐声朗读亲爱精诚。
examples.en: At graduation the cadets recited 'affection and sincerity' together.

usage.en: A four-character motto rather than a classical idiom. Since 1924 it has been the motto of the Whampoa (Huangpu) Academy and is still used by the military academy in Taiwan. The wording is usually credited to Sun Yat-sen's circle, but who first formulated it is not firmly settled, so no origin is given.
usage.zh: 四字校训，不是典故成语。自1924年起为黄埔军校校训，今天台湾的陆军军官学校仍沿用。通常认为出自孙中山一派，但最初由谁拟定并无定论，故不标出处。

pinyin: qián fāng chī jǐn, hòu fāng jǐn chī
literal: front · line · in · crisis, rear · area · tightly · eat
natural: the front is in crisis while the rear feasts

meaning.en: A wartime quip contrasting soldiers' hardship at the front with officials' feasting and corruption behind the lines.
meaning.zh: 战时的讽刺话：前线战事吃紧，后方官员却大吃大喝、贪污腐败。

equivalents: a feast behind the lines while the front bleeds

examples.zh: 抗战后期流行一句讽刺话：“前方吃紧，后方紧吃。”
examples.en: In the later war years a satirical saying spread: 'the front is in crisis while the rear feasts'.

examples.zh: 前方吃紧，后方紧吃，百姓对此怨声载道。
examples.en: With the front in crisis and the rear feasting, ordinary people complained bitterly.

usage.en: A pun built on 吃紧 ('be in crisis') and 紧吃 ('eat greedily'). Popular in the Nationalist-held areas around 1940-45 as a comment on official corruption. Also used today, often humorously, for any situation where leaders enjoy themselves while others struggle. No known author.
usage.zh: 利用“吃紧”与“紧吃”的字序对调构成的双关。1940至1945年前后流行于国统区，讽刺官员腐败。今天也常幽默地用于领导享乐而下面辛苦的场合。作者不详。

text: 一年准备，两年反攻，三年扫荡，五年成功
pinyin: yī nián zhǔn bèi, liǎng nián fǎn gōng, sān nián sǎo dàng, wǔ nián chéng gōng
literal: one · year · prepare, two · years · counter-attack, three · years · mop up, five · years · succeed
natural: one year to prepare, two to counter-attack, three to sweep, five to succeed

meaning.en: A Kuomintang slogan from the early 1950s in Taiwan, setting a timetable for retaking the mainland; the plan was never carried out.
meaning.zh: 1950年代初国民党在台湾提出的口号，为“反攻大陆”订出时间表，但始终没有实现。

equivalents: a five-year plan to retake the mainland

examples.zh: 教科书介绍了“一年准备，两年反攻，三年扫荡，五年成功”的口号。
examples.en: The textbook introduces the slogan 'one year to prepare, two to counter-attack, three to sweep, five to succeed'.

examples.zh: 一年准备，两年反攻，三年扫荡，五年成功，这个目标最终没有实现。
examples.en: The goal of 'one year to prepare, two to counter-attack, three to sweep, five to succeed' was never achieved.

usage.en: A historical slogan of the Nationalist government after its move to Taiwan, associated with Chiang Kai-shek's call to 'recover the mainland'. Now cited as a historical reference or, ironically, for an over-optimistic timetable. No origin is given.
usage.zh: 国民政府迁台后的历史口号，与蒋介石“反攻大陆”的主张相联系。今天作历史引用，或反讽过于乐观的时间表。不标出处。

pinyin: yǐ dǎng zhì guó
natural: govern the state through the party

meaning.en: The principle of Kuomintang 'party rule' in the Nanjing period, under which the party leads and supervises the government.
meaning.zh: 国民党在南京时期的“党治”原则：由政党领导和监督政府。

examples.zh: 南京国民政府时期实行“以党治国”。
examples.en: During the Nanjing government period 'rule by party' was practised.

examples.zh: 论文讨论了以党治国理念的由来。
examples.en: The paper discusses the origins of the idea of 'governing the state through the party'.

usage.en: A historical-political term associated with the period of political tutelage (训政) from 1928. Neutral, formal; studied in history and political science. No origin is given.
usage.zh: 与1928年起的训政时期相联系的历史政治术语。中性，正式，见于历史和政治学研究。不标出处。

synonyms: 一个主义，一个党，一个领袖

pinyin: huáng pǔ jīng shén
natural: the Whampoa spirit

meaning.en: The ethos of the Whampoa Military Academy, founded in Guangzhou in 1924: patriotism, discipline and readiness to sacrifice.
meaning.zh: 1924年在广州创办的黄埔军校所倡导的精神：爱国、守纪律、敢于牺牲。

examples.zh: 纪念馆的展览讲述了黄埔精神的形成。
examples.en: The museum's exhibition tells how the Whampoa spirit took shape.

examples.zh: 校友们常谈起黄埔精神，强调团结和奉献。
examples.en: Alumni often talk of the Whampoa spirit, stressing unity and devotion.

usage.en: Refers to the academy founded in 1924 with Sun Yat-sen's backing and the Soviet advisers' help, with Chiang Kai-shek as commandant; both Nationalist and Communist leaders taught or studied there. The term is used on both sides of the Taiwan Strait. Often associated with the motto 亲爱精诚.
usage.zh: 指1924年在孙中山支持、苏联顾问协助下创办、蒋介石任校长的黄埔军校；国共两党的许多人物都曾在此任教或学习。海峡两岸都使用这个说法，常与校训“亲爱精诚”联系在一起。

pinyin: kē xué jiù guó
natural: save the nation through science

meaning.en: The early twentieth-century belief that modern science and technology would make China strong again.
meaning.zh: 二十世纪初的主张：发展现代科学技术能使中国重新强盛。

examples.zh: 他留学归来，抱着科学救国的理想办起了实验室。
examples.en: Back from abroad, he set up a laboratory with the ideal of saving the nation through science.

examples.zh: 许多早期科学家怀着科学救国的志向。
examples.en: Many early scientists were driven by the aim of saving the nation through science.

usage.en: A historical idea of the May Fourth era ('Mr Science'), alongside 实业救国 and 教育救国. Today mostly a historical reference or an idealistic motto for scientists. No origin is given.
usage.zh: 五四时期（“赛先生”）流行的主张，与实业救国、教育救国并称。今天多作历史引用，或作科学工作者的理想口号。不标出处。

pinyin: jiào yù jiù guó
natural: save the nation through education

meaning.en: The belief that raising the people's education is the way to strengthen the nation.
meaning.zh: 主张通过提高国民教育水平来使国家富强。

examples.zh: 陶行知怀着教育救国的理想，创办了乡村学校。
examples.en: Tao Xingzhi, with the ideal of saving the nation through education, founded rural schools.

examples.zh: 民国时期许多人投身教育救国。
examples.en: In the Republican period many people devoted themselves to saving the nation through education.

usage.en: A historical idea popular in the late Qing and Republican years, linked with figures such as 蔡元培 and 陶行知, and often named next to 实业救国 and 科学救国. Today a historical reference or a motto for teachers.
usage.zh: 晚清和民国时期流行的主张，与蔡元培、陶行知等人相联系，常与实业救国、科学救国并提。今天作历史引用或教师的自勉之语。
